title: Cookbook:Bizcochito (Cinnamon Anise Cookies) I
steps: Cream the lard, sugar, and anise in a large mixing bowl. Add eggs and beat well.
Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
Alternately add flour to creamed mixture until a stiff dough has formed.
Knead dough slightly. Pat ¼–½ inch (0.5–1 cm) thick or roll to a ¼–½ inch (0.5–1 cm) diameter log.
Bake in an oven preheated to 350°F (180°C) for 10–12 minutes or until golden brown.
Dust, while still hot, with cinnamon sugar.

A '''bizcochito''' or '''biscochito''' is a crispy [[:Category:Cookie recipes|cookie]] flavored with [[Cookbook:Anise|anise]] and [[Cookbook:cinnamon|cinnamon]]. It was developed by Hispanic residents of New Mexico and southern Colorado who trace their ancestry back to the first Spanish colonists. The recipe for making the cookie has been influenced not only by local and indigenous customs, but also by cookie recipes brought to New Mexico with immigrants from other countries. It is served at special celebrations such as wedding receptions, baptisms and religious holidays, especially Christmas. It is usually eaten with morning [[Cookbook:coffee|coffee]] or milk, and after lunch and dinner when it is served as a dessert. The cookie is little known outside the Southwest.

There is no "official" recipe for making bizcochitos. Each region, and often each family, has its own distinct recipe for baking the cookies, including some that add wine or whiskey. This recipe is from southern New Mexico. 

== Ingredients ==
*1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] (500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) pure [[Cookbook:lard|lard]]
*1½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (150 g) white granulated [[Cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] (20 g) [[Cookbook:Anise|anise seed]] (crushed)
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], beaten
*3 ⅓ cups (400 g) [[Cookbook:flour|flour]]
*3 tsp (30 g) [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
*1 tsp (10 g) [[Cookbook:salt|salt]] 
* [[Cookbook:Sugar|Cinnamon sugar]] for topping

== Procedure ==
#[[Cookbook:Creaming|Cream]] the lard, sugar, and anise in a large mixing bowl. Add eggs and beat well.
#Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a large mixing bowl.
#Alternately add flour to creamed mixture until a stiff dough has formed.
#Knead dough slightly. Pat ¼–½ inch (0.5–1 cm) thick or roll to a ¼–½ inch (0.5–1 cm) diameter log.
#Cut into desired shapes.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in an [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] preheated to 350°F (180°C) for 10–12 minutes or until golden brown.
#Dust, while still hot, with cinnamon sugar.
#Let cool.
